overview.summary: Binary Search is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that finds a target in a sorted array in O(log N) time by repeatedly halving the search space.
learningObjectives: Understand why the array MUST be sorted.
Master the mid-point calculation to avoid integer overflow.
Identify the three main templates of Binary Search (exact match, lower bound, upper bound).
overview.interviewRelevance: Binary search is the ultimate optimization when a brute-force O(N) scan is too slow. Finding the O(log N) solution is a mandatory interview milestone.

paragraphs: Imagine guessing a number between 1 and 100. If you guess 50 and I say 'Higher!', you instantly eliminate 1 through 50. You don't need to check them.
By always guessing in the exact middle of the remaining possibilities, you can find the answer in a maximum of 7 guesses instead of 100.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: Every single comparison eliminates exactly half of the remaining data.

definition.technicalDefinition: Binary Search is a search algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted array by comparing the target value to the middle element of the array.

vocabulary.definition: The range of indices `[left, right]` where the target might still exist.
The index exactly halfway between the current `left` and `right` boundaries.
O(log N). The time increases linearly only as the data size increases exponentially.

keyProperties: Requires random access (like an Array, not a Linked List).
Requires the data to be sorted (or at least monotonic).
Reduces search space by 50% on every iteration.

metaphor: A dictionary. To find 'Monkey', you open to the middle ('M'). You know instantly whether to search the left half or right half of the book.
mentalModel.clickSentence: If you know it's not in the left half, you never have to look at the left half again.

memoryDescription: Binary Search requires zero extra memory. It operates entirely in-place.
It simply maintains two integer pointers: `left` and `right`.

memoryLayout.label: Left Pointer
memoryLayout.value: Tracks the start of the valid window.

memoryLayout.label: Right Pointer
memoryLayout.value: Tracks the end of the valid window.

operations.name: Calculate Midpoint
operations.description: Find the center. Use `left + (right - left) // 2` instead of `(left + right) // 2` to prevent integer overflow in languages like Java/C++.
operations.visualNote: A pointer drops exactly in the middle of the active window.

operations.name: Adjust Boundaries
operations.description: If mid is too small, move `left` past mid. If mid is too big, move `right` behind mid.
operations.visualNote: Half of the array greys out, completely eliminated from the search.

patternTemplate.pseudocode:
left = 0
right = N - 1
while left <= right:
  mid = left + (right - left) // 2
  if arr[mid] == target: return mid
  if arr[mid] < target: left = mid + 1
  else: right = mid - 1
return -1
patternTemplate.whenToUse: Whenever an array is sorted and you need to find an element, or when searching for an optimal numerical answer within a known range ('Binary Search on Answer').

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You are given a sorted array of 100,000 integers and a target value. Return the index if the target is found.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: The array is already SORTED. Any time you see a sorted array and a search task, Binary Search is the intended O(log N) optimal approach.

examples.title: Binary Search
examples.problemStatement: Given an array of integers nums which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. If target exists, then return its index. Otherwise, return -1.
steps: If nums[mid] < target, target must be to the right, so left = mid + 1.
If nums[mid] > target, target must be to the left, so right = mid - 1.
examples.rationale: This is the purest form of the pattern.

conceptQuiz.question: Why use `left + (right - left) / 2` instead of `(left + right) / 2`?
options: To prevent integer overflow if left and right are very large numbers.
conceptQuiz.explanation: If left and right are near the 32-bit integer limit (2.14 billion), adding them together `(left + right)` will overflow into a negative number before the division happens, causing a crash.

conceptQuiz.question: What is the condition for the standard while loop in Binary Search?
conceptQuiz.explanation: Using `<=` ensures that we check the element even when `left` and `right` converge onto the exact same index.

practice.title: Search Insert Position
practice.keyInsight: When the loop breaks, `left` will be exactly at the correct insertion index.

practice.title: First Bad Version
practice.keyInsight: Use `while left < right` and don't skip mid when moving the right pointer.

practice.title: Koko Eating Bananas
practice.keyInsight: Binary Search on the Answer. Guess a speed, check if it works, adjust.
